Graduate Admissions and Academics
60+ doctoral programs. 80+ master’s and professional programs. One world-class research university.
At WashU, graduate and professional students work alongside world-renowned faculty, engage in groundbreaking research, and join a collaborative community dedicated to solving society’s most pressing challenges. Whether you’re pursuing a master’s, doctoral, or professional degree, you’ll find the resources, mentorship, and opportunities to help you reach your goals.
Find Your Place
WashU offers graduate and professional programs across nine schools and disciplines spanning the humanities, social sciences, sciences, engineering, business, public health, social work, law, medicine, and design.

In addition to the eight schools listed above, WashU offers a professional and continuing education division, School of Continuing & Professional Studies (CAPS), giving adult students the opportunity to experience the excitement of attending and earning a degree or certificate from a world-class research institution.
Applying to WashU
Required application materials, application fees and deadlines vary by program. Please check with your admitting department of interest to you to confirm these requirements.
Application Materials
WashU graduate and professional programs typically require:
A completed online application
A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution (or equivalent international credential)
Official or unofficial academic transcripts, depending on program requirements
A resume or curriculum vitae (CV)
Letters of recommendation
A statement of purpose or personal statement
For international students: confirmation of English Language Proficiency (see below)
Additional materials, including but not limited to portfolios, writing samples, interviews, prerequisite coursework, or standardized test scores, may be required by specific programs.
Applicants are encouraged to submit materials well in advance of posted deadlines to ensure timely review. Required application materials, application fees, and deadlines vary by program. Please contact the department of interest if you have any questions or to confirm required materials.
Admissions Policies
English Language Proficiency
International students for whom English is not the first language are required to submit official English language proficiency test scores as part of their application for admission.
WashU accepted tests and minimum score requirements:
Duolingo English Test (DET) – 125 minimum overall score
GATEWAY English Test – 495 minimum overall score
International English Language Testing System (IELTS) Academic – 6.5 minimum composite score
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) iBT – 5.0 overall (new scale) OR 4.5 ≥ 90 overall (old scale)
WashU does not accept super-scored results (a combination of the highest scored sections) such as TOEFL MyBest.
Official test scores must be received by WashU directly from the test administration agency. Official scores must be less than two years old at the time of application deadline or submission of application. Admitted students who defer enrollment may need to submit new scores if their previously submitted scores have expired.
Program-based Score Requirements
Some schools and programs may have higher test score requirements than the university minimum requirements based on the level of English proficiency needed for their respective course of study and/or program. Individuals should consult with the school and/or program to which they are applying to confirm the score requirements for their respective program.
Individuals may be required by their school or academic department to complete English language placement assessments and/or courses or programming for English communication support.
Exemptions
Exemptions from the English language proficiency test requirement may be granted for individuals who meet one or more of the following criteria:
Citizenship from one of the following countries: Australia, Bermuda, Cameroon, Canada, Caribbean Commonwealth countries and British Caribbean territories (Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, The Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, Montserrat, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Trinidad and Tobago, Turks and Caicos Islands), Ghana, Gibraltar, Hong Kong, India, Ireland, Kenya, Liberia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Singapore, South Africa, Uganda, United Kingdom, United States, Zambia, Zimbabwe.
Earned the equivalent of a bachelor’s degree* or master’s degree (before matriculation at WashU) within the past five (5) years from an institution in one of the following countries: Australia, Bermuda, Cameroon, Canada, Caribbean Commonwealth countries and British Caribbean territories (Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, The Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, Montserrat, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Trinidad and Tobago, Turks and Caicos Islands), Ghana, Gibraltar, Hong Kong, India, Ireland, Kenya, Liberia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Singapore, South Africa, Uganda, United Kingdom, United States, Zambia, Zimbabwe.
Earned the equivalent of a bachelor’s degree* (before matriculation at WashU) within the past five (5) years at an English-medium institution in one of the following countries: Botswana, Burundi, Christmas Island, Cook Islands, Curacao, Eritrea, Fiji, The Gambia, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Malta, Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Namibia, Niue, Norfolk Island, Northern Mariana Islands, Pakistan, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Pitcairn Islands, Rwanda, Samoa, Seychelles, Sint Maarten, Solomon Islands, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Tuvalu, Vanuatu.
Possesses two (2) years or more of continuous full-time work experience in the United States within the last five (5) years.
For J-1 exchange visitors:
Earned a minimum Cambridge English scale score of 180 on Cambridge C2 Proficiency (formerly CPE), Cambridge C1 Advanced (formerly CAE) or Cambridge B2 First (formerly FCE);
Earned a minimum score of 3.0 on the English3 Interview (applies to J-1 scholars only in the following categories: short-term scholar, research scholar, professor, student intern, specialist);
Partner university confirms that the prospective student has passed an English proficiency test in alignment with WashU English language proficiency requirements (applies to J-1 exchange students only in the following categories: non-degree student).
Appropriate documentation based on the type of exemption requested will be required. Note that any exemption request from this Policy is reviewed on a case-by-case basis and must be approved by the Senior Vice Provost for Graduate Education and International Affairs after review of the entire record.
*For joint (dual, 2+2, etc.) programs in which the medium of instruction was English at one institution and the medium of instruction was not English at the other institution, exemptions will be made for applicants whose studies were in English for a minimum of two (2) years (within the past five (5) years) regardless of physical location.
Costs & Funding Your Education
Tuition
Graduate and professional program tuition rates are established by individual schools and programs and may vary based on enrollment status, program requirements, and other factors. Applicants should contact their program’s admissions office for information.
Funding Your Education
Program-Specific Funding Opportunities
Many schools and programs offer funding opportunities that are unique to their students. These may include scholarships, fellowships, assistantships, tuition awards, stipends, grants, and professional development funding. Applicants should contact their program’s admissions office for information about funding opportunities available.
University-Wide Funding Opportunities
WashU offers a variety of funding resources available to graduate and professional students across disciplines including the Olin-Chancellor’s Fellowship. Find more information here.
Academic Calendars
The academic calendars are available on the Office of the University Registrar’s website.
